From 23484d817082c3005252d8edfc8292c8a1006b5b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Rouven Czerwinski <r.czerwinski@pengutronix.de>
Date: Thu, 7 Dec 2023 08:58:36 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: rfkill: gpio: set GPIO direction

Fix the undefined usage of the GPIO consumer API after retrieving the
GPIO description with GPIO_ASIS. The API documentation mentions that
GPIO_ASIS won't set a GPIO direction and requires the user to set a
direction before using the GPIO.

This can be confirmed on i.MX6 hardware, where rfkill-gpio is no longer
able to enabled/disable a device, presumably because the GPIO controller
was never configured for the output direction.

Fixes: b2f750c3a80b ("net: rfkill: gpio: prevent value glitch during probe")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Rouven Czerwinski <r.czerwinski@pengutronix.de>
Link: https://msgid.link/20231207075835.3091694-1-r.czerwinski@pengutronix.de
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>

diff --git a/net/rfkill/rfkill-gpio.c b/net/rfkill/rfkill-gpio.c
index 5a81505fba9a..4e32d659524e 100644
--- a/net/rfkill/rfkill-gpio.c
+++ b/net/rfkill/rfkill-gpio.c
@@ -126,6 +126,14 @@ static int rfkill_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 
+	ret = gpiod_direction_output(rfkill->reset_gpio, true);
+	if (ret)
+		return ret;
+
+	ret = gpiod_direction_output(rfkill->shutdown_gpio, true);
+	if (ret)
+		return ret;
+
 	rfkill->rfkill_dev = rfkill_alloc(rfkill->name, &pdev->dev,
 					  rfkill->type, &rfkill_gpio_ops,
 					  rfkill);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/rfkill/rfkill-gpio.c`**
- Added two lines of code to set the GPIO direction for `reset_gpio` and `shutdown_gpio` using the `gpiod_direction_output` function.
- The code checks the return value of `gpiod_direction_output` for both GPIOs and returns an error if the direction setting fails.

### Relationships
The modifications in `rfkill-gpio.c` address a bug related to the undefined usage of the GPIO consumer API when using `GPIO_ASIS`. By explicitly setting the GPIO direction for both `reset_gpio` and `shutdown_gpio`, the patch ensures that the GPIO controller is properly configured for output, which resolves the issue of the rfkill-gpio not being able to enable/disable a device on i.MX6 hardware. This change is a direct response to the problem identified in the previous commit referenced in the patch.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
gpio = devm_gpiod_get_optional(&pdev->dev, "reset", GPIOD_ASIS);
gpio = devm_gpiod_get_optional(&pdev->dev, "shutdown", GPIOD_ASIS);
```
Reason:
The use of `GPIOD_ASIS` when retrieving the GPIO descriptors does not set the GPIO direction, which means that the GPIOs are not configured for output. This results in the inability of the rfkill-gpio to enable or disable the device on i.MX6 hardware.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
ret = gpiod_direction_output(rfkill->reset_gpio, true);
ret = gpiod_direction_output(rfkill->shutdown_gpio, true);
```
Reason:
These statements explicitly set the direction of the GPIOs to output, ensuring that the GPIO controller is properly configured to enable or disable the device, thus resolving the issue caused by the previous undefined usage of the GPIO consumer API.
